subject: Re: Private listing MSA - performance & uptime language
messages:
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@gentech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@gentech.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private listing MSA - performance & uptime language

Jordan —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We're excited about the private listing but Legal/Procurement flagged a few items in the MSA and the SLA that we need clarified before we can move to signature:

1) SLA measurable availability: we currently see a 99.5% uptime in the draft. For our clinical workloads we need at least 99.9% or a defined credit schedule.
2) Remedies: the credit language is vague; procurement wants a concrete calculation and cap.
3) Data residency: confirmation that all inference workloads and logs for Gentech will remain in the us-east region.
4) Subprocessor list + 30-day notification for changes.

Attaching our SOW (Gentech_Master_SOW_v2.pdf) and redlined points. Can your team propose language that maps to our commercial team expectation (credit schedule + max cap)?

Best,
Amir
Procurement Manager, Gentech Health

Attachment: Gentech_Master_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private listing MSA - performance & uptime language

Amir —

Thanks for the clear list. I looped in Marissa (commercial) and Kimberly (legal) to draft proposed language. Initial thoughts:

- We can move to a 99.9% availability target for the configuration tied to a Dedicated capacity SKU; for Hosted (shared) we need to keep 99.5% but can offer an SLA uplift as a priced add-on.
- Credit schedule: propose credits equal to 5% of monthly service fees for each 0.1% below 99.9%, capped at 50% of the monthly fee — we can model examples for you.
- Data residency: we can guarantee inference and log residency in US-EAST region for private listings with a contractual clause plus onboarding checklist to validate.
- Subprocessors: we will provide current list and 30-day notice for changes; longer notice for sensitive subprocessors.

Attaching our clean MSA and an SLA appendix draft (Redwood_MSA_clean.docx, SLA_appendix_draft.xlsx). Kimberly — can you propose the exact credit language that lines up with what Sales is proposing? Marissa — can you confirm commercial acceptance of the cap?

Next step: I'll set up a 30-minute call with your procurement/legal to walk the proposed wording.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Manager, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private listing MSA - performance & uptime language

Jordan / Marissa —

Draft language below that I recommend inserting into the SLA appendix. Happy to iterate but wanted to get something concrete in the thread for Amir: 

"Service Availability. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Service available 99.9% of the time during each monthly billing period for Dedicated Private listing configurations. For Hosted private listings where capacity is shared across customers, Redwood targets 99.5% availability. Availability will be measured based on successful API request responses excluding scheduled maintenance and changes mutually agreed in advance.

Service Credits. If Redwood fails to meet the Service Availability for a given monthly billing period, Customer may be eligible to receive a credit applied to the monthly fees as follows: 5% credit of the monthly fee for each 0.1% below the applicable Availability target, rounded to the nearest tenth, up to a maximum aggregate credit equal to 50% of the monthly fee for that billing period. Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures. Credits will not be payable in cash and will be applied against future invoices.

Measurement and Exceptions. Credits will not be applied where downtime is caused by Customer configurations, customer data issues, force majeure, or third-party components outside Redwood's reasonable control. Redwood will provide a monthly availability report upon Customer request for the prior three months."

Also recommend: add a clause guaranteeing data residency (US-East) with audit rights limited to evidence and redacted logs, plus a procedural requirement for subprocessor notification (30 days).

If that works, Jordan please send to Amir and propose the call.

-Kim
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@gentech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@gentech.com>, procurement@gentech.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private listing MSA - performance & uptime language

Jordan / Kim —

Thanks — the draft SLA language is clear and close. A couple of follow ups from Legal: 

- The credit cap at 50% is acceptable to our CFO if we can include a 12-month lookback / aggregation clause (i.e., credits across a 12-month period cannot exceed 100% of one month's fees) — can you confirm?
- For measurement, we need the definition of "scheduled maintenance" and a maximum total maintenance window per quarter (suggest 8 hours).
- Data residency: we need an execution commitment (exhibit) and a verification checklist during onboarding.

Also can we schedule the call for Friday 25th at 11:00am PT to finalize? Sofia from Legal will join.

Best,
Amir
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@gentech.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@gentech.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private listing MSA - performance & uptime language

Amir / Sofia —

Thanks for the feedback. Confirming next steps and responses for the Friday call: 

1) Credit aggregation: Redwood can accept a 12-month aggregation cap: credits may not exceed 100% of one month's fees in aggregate across any 12-month rolling period. We'll document that in the SLA.
2) Scheduled maintenance: we'll define scheduled maintenance as planned maintenance windows announced at least 72 hours in advance; Redwood will not schedule more than 8 hours of maintenance affecting availability in any calendar quarter without Customer consent.
3) Data residency: we'll include an onboarding exhibit and a one-time verification checklist; ongoing log access will be redacted and limited to metadata and non-PII telemetry.

Call confirmed: Fri, 25 Jun 2027, 11:00am PT / 14:00 ET. I'll circulate a dial-in and the updated appendix prior to the call (SLA_appendix_draft.xlsx updated).

Look forward to finalizing.

Jordan Blake
Senior Manager, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
